affirmation-is-not-love.metaDescription: Therapeutic culture taught us that to love someone is to confirm them.

qa.question: Is Affirmation the Same as Love?
qa.answer: Therapeutic culture taught us that to love someone is to confirm them. But real love wills the good of the other, and sometimes that means telling the truth they do not want to hear. A pastor on the difference, and why it costs.

authority-we-traded-for-authenticity.metaDescription: Somewhere in the last few decades a sentence changed shape in the Christian mouth. The old sentence was 'the Bible says.'

qa.question: Is the Bible the Final Word, or Am I?
qa.answer: Somewhere in the last few decades a sentence changed shape in the Christian mouth. The old sentence was 'the Bible says.' The new one is 'I feel like God is.' We thought we were gaining freedom. We were changing kings.

cheap-grace-left-hand.metaDescription: Bonhoeffer's cheap grace is usually aimed at the easy-believism of the right.

conscience-outsourced-to-party.metaDescription: We talk about the church captured by the political right. A pastor on the conscience we handed our tribe without ever signing the papers.

qa.question: Should a Christian Follow a Political Party?
qa.answer: We talk about the church captured by the political right. The left's version is harder to see, because the left believes it is the side that thinks for itself. A pastor on the conscience we handed our tribe without ever signing the papers.

deconstruction-without-reconstruction.metaDescription: The exvangelical wave got the diagnosis right. The wounds are real and the church earned most of them.

qa.question: What Happens After You Deconstruct Your Faith?
qa.answer: The exvangelical wave got the diagnosis right. The wounds are real and the church earned most of them. But deconstructing your faith and never rebuilding is not freedom, it is an empty house, and empty houses do not stay empty.

right-side-of-history.metaDescription: "The right side of history" is the most successful piece of secular theology of our age, and the American church swallowed it whole.

the-sin-we-stopped-naming.metaDescription: Progressive Christianity recovered structural sin and called it justice.

when-justice-becomes-a-gospel.metaDescription: Is social justice biblical? Yes, which is exactly why it makes such a convincing god.

nostalgia-is-not-the-kingdom.metaDescription: The longing for a lost Christian America feels like faith and works like idolatry.

qa.question: Was America Ever Really a Christian Nation?
qa.answer: The longing for a lost Christian America feels like faith and works like idolatry. It is the mirror image of the progressive worship of the future, a moment on the calendar mistaken for the kingdom of God.

six-verses-we-memorized.metaDescription: A tribe does not have to delete a single verse to edit the Bible. It only has to decide which ones get printed in bold.

strongman-theology.metaDescription: A frightened church always asks for a king. We are praying the same prayer. The elders did not ask for a tyrant. That is the part everyone misses.

the-flag-in-the-sanctuary.metaDescription: The flag standing beside the cross did not arrive by accident, and it did not arrive in the New Testament.

qa.question: Why Is There a Flag in the Sanctuary?
qa.answer: The flag standing beside the cross did not arrive by accident, and it did not arrive in the New Testament. A pastor traces how American civil religion fused God and nation, and why the seam should worry the people who love both.

the-persecution-we-invented.metaDescription: A church that ran the culture for a thousand years lost the room and called it persecution.

qa.question: Is the American Church Really Being Persecuted?
qa.answer: A church that ran the culture for a thousand years lost the room and called it persecution. Here is what that word costs us, and what the actual persecuted church would say if we let them speak.

the-third-temptation.metaDescription: In the wilderness, Satan offered Jesus all the kingdoms of the world if he would bow. Power was always the temptation.

two-kingdoms-one-pledge.metaDescription: You cannot pledge ultimate allegiance twice. Allegiance. It is not a soft word.

qa.question: Can You Pledge Allegiance to Two Kingdoms?
qa.answer: You cannot pledge ultimate allegiance twice. A pastor on the two-kingdoms tradition, the cost of following a crucified King, and why the line between Caesar and Christ runs straight through the American Christian's chest.

when-the-pulpit-became-a-precinct.metaDescription: A church does not have to endorse a candidate to become a precinct. It only has to make the tribe feel at home and the outsider feel watched.

proof-texting.metaDescription: A verse for every argument and an argument for every verse. Proof-texting lets both tribes win every debate while Scripture itself disappears.

reading-in-community.metaDescription: A tribe agrees with you. A community corrects you. Both gather around the Bible. Both pray. Both feel like fellowship.

six-lenses-that-distort-the-bible.metaDescription: You think you read the Bible plainly. Here is how to see the glass before it edits the text.

the-whole-counsel.metaDescription: Cherry-picking is the American hermeneutic. We keep the verses that fit, lose the ones that don't, and call the leftovers our faith.

what-the-original-audience-heard.metaDescription: The first hearers of the Good Samaritan would have flinched at a word you read right past.

christendom-is-ending.metaDescription: For seventeen centuries, being born in the West meant being born Christian. That arrangement is dying, and most of the church is grieving the wrong thing.

exile-is-not-the-end.metaDescription: The church in the West keeps treating its loss of cultural power as a catastrophe.

the-numbers-behind-the-decline.metaDescription: The statistics about the dying church get quoted in two directions, apocalypse and denial, and both are usually wrong.

what-dies-when-christendom-dies.metaDescription: Not everything that is dying in the church deserves to be mourned. When something large dies, the first grief is indiscriminate.

witness-without-power.metaDescription: The early church conquered the Roman Empire without a single seat in its government.

discipling-people-out-of-fear.metaDescription: Political capture runs on fear, and you cannot argue a frightened person back to peace.

pastoring-a-captured-congregation.metaDescription: Your people are being discipled forty hours a week by a screen that knows them better than you do.

qa.question: How Do You Pastor a Church Addicted to Cable News?
qa.answer: Your people are being discipled forty hours a week by a screen that knows them better than you do. A working pastor on shepherding a congregation whose first language has quietly become cable news.

preaching-to-a-divided-room.metaDescription: Half your room is braced for you to betray them and the other half is hoping you will.

the-last-nonpartisan-in-the-room.metaDescription: Everyone wants to know which side you are on, and refusing to say it costs you something real.

when-elders-are-loyal-to-a-party.metaDescription: The capture that endangers a church most is not in the pews. It is on the board.

burnout-is-not-a-badge.metaDescription: We turned exhaustion into a virtue and then wondered why our best men kept collapsing. The empty man is not the faithful man.

the-loneliest-room-in-the-church.metaDescription: The fullest building in town has one room where a man sits alone with everything he is not allowed to say.

the-pastor-nobody-checks-on.metaDescription: We built a vocation where the man who asks everyone how they are gets asked by no one. Here is how the grammar got that way, and what it takes to break it.

when-the-calling-costs-more.metaDescription: No one lied to us about the calling. They just never finished the sentence about the bill, and the second invoice has names and dates the first one didn't.

why-pastors-quit.metaDescription: Most pastors do not quit on the bad day. They quit on the ordinary one, after a long erosion no one watched happen.

emotional-labor-in-marriage.metaDescription: What emotional labor and the mental load really are, why one spouse ends up carrying them, why children deepen the gap, and what Scripture asks of both.

qa.question: Why Does One Spouse Carry the Whole Mental Load in Marriage?
qa.answer: The heaviest work in many marriages is not the chores but the watch: the anticipating and remembering that leaves no trace when it is done well. Children multiply it, and Scripture has always called it work that both spouses owe.

the-resentment-in-your-marriage.metaDescription: What resentment in marriage means, when a grievance is fair and when it turns to bitterness, and how Scripture moves from honest speech to forgiveness.

the-slow-drift-that-ends-marriages.metaDescription: Why couples drift apart and end up like roommates: the old sin of acedia, the modern soulmate marriage, and how Scripture calls spouses back to attention.

what-silence-costs-a-marriage.metaDescription: Why the silent treatment wounds a marriage, when silence protects or listens instead, and what Scripture, Bonhoeffer and Gottman teach about talking again.

qa.question: Where are you?
qa.answer: The first question God asks a human being in Scripture is asked of a man who has gone silent. "But the LORD God called to the man and said to him, 'Where are you?'" (Genesis 3:9). God isn't lost. The man is. And God doesn't accept the silence as the new arrangement. He comes looking, with a question rather than a charge, which leaves room for an answer, and he walks through the hedge of leaves and trees not to shame the man but to draw him back into speech.

what-the-bible-says-about-submission.metaDescription: Ephesians 5 read in context: mutual submission, headship defined by the cross, both main Christian views, and why submission never requires enduring abuse.

qa.question: What Does the Bible Say About Submission in Marriage?
qa.answer: Ephesians 5 begins a sentence earlier than it is usually quoted, and its heaviest command falls on the husband. Read whole, it gives no one a license to dominate and no one permission to hide.

when-you-married-someone-you-no-longer-r.metaDescription: Why spouses become strangers, especially once the kids leave, what growing apart does and does not mean, and why the marriage vow was made for this season.

qa.question: I Don't Recognize My Spouse Anymore. Is the Marriage Over?
qa.answer: The stranger across the table is not proof the marriage failed. Both of you changed, as every vow assumed you would, and the question is whether you will learn the person who is actually there, including the one in the mirror.

discipline-without-domination.metaDescription: What biblical discipline means: paideia in Ephesians and Hebrews, the rod in Proverbs read as wisdom, the spanking debate, and correcting without anger.

family-devotions-authentic.metaDescription: How to do family devotions and teach kids to pray and read the Bible: what Scripture asks of a home, what history shows, and what tired parents can keep.

how-to-talk-kids-faith-doubt.metaDescription: How to pass on faith to your kids when you have doubts: what Scripture says, what research on handing down faith found, and why honesty outlasts theater.

raising-kids-who-think.metaDescription: How to answer kids' hard questions about God: why Scripture expects children to ask, what the catechisms knew, and why owned questions outlast recitation.

raising-sons-manhood.metaDescription: Your son is being handed two false manhoods and told to pick one. One inflates him, one erases him. Neither one is the cross.

teenager-losing-faith.metaDescription: Your first instinct will be to win the argument. The argument is not the thing your teenager is testing. You are.

the-pastors-kids-are-watching.metaDescription: Your congregation hears your sermons. Your children watch the drive home.

the-weight-of-what-you-model.metaDescription: Your children are not listening to your instructions. They are watching your reflexes, and the reflexes are the curriculum.

the-work-nobody-watches.metaDescription: The culture calls mothering a waste of a mind. The church hands it a carnation one Sunday a year and loads it like a mule the other fifty-one.

can-you-have-faith-and-doubt.metaDescription: You were told real Christians do not have questions. The Hebrew word for faith says the opposite: not certainty, but a steadiness that can carry weight.

qa.question: Can You Have Faith and Still Have Doubts?
qa.answer: You were told a real Christian does not have questions. The Hebrew word underneath faith says the opposite. Emunah is not certainty, it is weight-bearing steadiness, the word used of Moses hands held up until sunset.

constantines-bargain.metaDescription: Much of what people leave when they leave the faith is not the faith at all.

dark-night-god-feels-absent.metaDescription: The silence is not punishment and it is not your failure. The tradition has a name for it, and the name is the beginning of surviving it.

depression-or-the-dark-night.metaDescription: On depression, the dark night of the soul, and the line no one should have to find alone. Fifteen years of pastoring keeps sending me the same two people.

excavation-not-demolition.metaDescription: Demolition and excavation use the same tools, the pry bar, the shovel, the refusal to respect a wall just because it is standing.

what-if-we-are-wrong.metaDescription: The question shows up at night: what if the whole thing is a story we told ourselves? A faith that cannot survive that question was never faith.

qa.question: What If Christianity Is Wrong?
qa.answer: The question arrives uninvited, usually at night: what if the whole thing is a story we told ourselves? A faith that cannot survive the question was never faith. It was shelter.

when-fear-rewrites-theology.metaDescription: Fear does not announce itself as fear. It tells you the worry is wisdom.

when-god-doesnt-make-sense.metaDescription: We were sold a God who would add up. The God of the Bible refuses the equation, and the refusal is not a flaw in the system.

why-does-god-feel-far-away.metaDescription: Feeling that God is far away is not a conclusion you reasoned your way to. It is the weather of our age. A pastor who came from atheism on why.

qa.question: Why Does God Feel So Far Away?
qa.answer: The sense that God is distant is not a conclusion you reasoned your way to. It is the weather of an age. A pastor who came to faith from atheism on disenchantment, the buffered self, and why the thinness you feel is the ceiling of a house rather than the edge of the world.

suffering-without-explanation.metaDescription: Everyone shows up with a reason for suffering. Job spends thirty seven chapters refusing every one, and when God finally speaks he gives none either.

qa.question: Why Does God Allow Suffering?
qa.answer: Everyone arrives with a reason. The book of Job spends thirty-seven chapters refusing every reason offered, and when God finally speaks, he never gives one either.

the-theology-of-saturday.metaDescription: We have a theology of the cross and a theology of the resurrection. We are very good at Friday and Sunday. We have almost nothing for Saturday.

qa.question: Where Is God on Holy Saturday?
qa.answer: We have a theology of the cross and a theology of the resurrection. We have almost nothing for the day in between, which is the day most of the grieving are actually living in.

the-weight-that-stays.metaDescription: You were promised the grief would lift. It did not lift. The literature of grief is full of stages, and the stages imply a destination.

what-psalms-teach-about-anger-at-god.metaDescription: The church taught you that anger at God is a sin. The prayer book God gave us is full of it, and his own Son died with a complaint on his lips.

qa.question: Is It Okay to Be Angry at God?
qa.answer: The church taught you that anger at God is a sin to repent of. The prayer book God gave us is full of it, and his own Son died with a complaint on his lips.

when-god-is-silent-and-the-room-is-empty.metaDescription: You prayed, and the ceiling gave nothing back. You learned the silence in stages. First the phone calls stopped. Then the casseroles stopped.

qa.question: Where Is God When You're Grieving?
qa.answer: You prayed, and the ceiling gave nothing back. This is what the church almost never says about the silence of God in grief, and why the silence is not the absence you fear it is.

the-faith-once-delivered.metaDescription: Most of what an American thinks of as 'Christianity' is a few generations old.

the-trinity-plainly.metaDescription: It sounds like a math problem the church flunked: one God, three persons. It was never math.

qa.question: How Can God Be Three and One?
qa.answer: It sounds like a math problem the church flunked: one God, three persons. It was never math. It is the church's best attempt to say everything true about a God who showed up in person.

what-the-creed-leaves-out.metaDescription: If you only knew Christians from the internet, you would think they agree on nothing.

why-christians-recite-creeds.metaDescription: Standing in a room of strangers, reciting words written before your country existed, sounds like the opposite of real faith.

qa.question: Why Would Anyone Recite a 1,700-Year-Old Creed?
qa.answer: Standing in a room of strangers, reciting words written before your country existed, sounds like the opposite of real faith. It is closer to the truth than 'just me and my Bible' ever was.

why-the-incarnation-matters.metaDescription: The Christmas story has been sentimentalized into harmlessness. The problem with the Christmas story is that you have heard it too many times to hear it.

easter-is-not-a-day.metaDescription: We treat Easter as a single morning, lilies, a sunrise service, ham by noon, done.

ordinary-time.metaDescription: The church year has two famous seasons and one long stretch nobody talks about, the green months between Pentecost and Advent called Ordinary Time.

what-is-advent.metaDescription: Advent is not the Christmas warm-up. It is four weeks the church spends in the dark, on purpose, waiting for a birth that happened two thousand years ago.

qa.question: What Is Advent, and Why Wait for Something That Already Happened?
qa.answer: Advent is not the Christmas warm-up. It is four weeks the church spends in the dark, on purpose, waiting for a birth that happened two thousand years ago. Once you understand why, you may find it is the most honest season there is.

why-lent.metaDescription: Giving up coffee or chocolate for six weeks looks like a quaint religious diet.

qa.question: Why Would Anyone Give Something Up for Lent?
qa.answer: Giving up coffee or chocolate for six weeks looks like a quaint religious diet. It is something far stranger and more serious: forty days of deliberately removing what numbs you, to find out what is actually underneath. Here is what Lent is really for.

why-the-church-has-a-calendar.metaDescription: You already live by a calendar, it tells you when to spend, when to hurry, when to want more. The church year tells a different story about time.

qa.question: Why Does the Church Have Its Own Calendar?
qa.answer: You already live by a calendar, it tells you when to spend, when to hurry, when to want more. The church year tells a different story about time. Here is what it is for, and what it does to you over years.

the-table-that-divides.metaDescription: The one meal Jesus left to hold his people together has become the thing that most visibly keeps them apart. A newcomer notices this fast.

what-happens-at-communion.metaDescription: A small piece of bread. A sip from a cup. Christians have argued for centuries about what it means and almost never about whether it matters.

qa.question: What Actually Happens at Communion?
qa.answer: A small piece of bread. A sip from a cup. Christians have argued for centuries about what it means and almost never about whether it matters. Here is what is going on when the church eats.

why-baptism.metaDescription: Water poured over a head, a few old words, and a person comes up changed, or so the church claims.

why-christians-confess-out-loud.metaDescription: Saying your worst out loud, to another person, in plain words, almost everything in us resists it.

why-faith-uses-physical-things.metaDescription: If Christianity is about the spirit and the soul, why is it so obsessed with stuff, water, bread, oil, wine, a body on a cross?

a-day-of-doing-nothing.metaDescription: Stopping for a full day, no work, no producing, no proving, feels almost impossible to a culture organized around output.

praying-at-fixed-hours.metaDescription: For most of Christian history, believers stopped what they were doing and prayed at set times of the day. They did not wait to feel like it.

reading-the-bible-slowly.metaDescription: We read everything fast now, including Scripture, skimming for the point, the takeaway, the verse to post.

silence-and-solitude.metaDescription: Sixteen hundred years ago, a handful of Christians walked into the desert to be alone and quiet.

why-christians-fast.metaDescription: Fasting was once as ordinary in Christian life as prayer. Then it quietly disappeared.

angels-demons-and-the-unseen.metaDescription: As a materialist this was the easiest thing in the Bible to mock, and later the thing I had understood least. Angels, demons, an unseen order.

anxiety-and-faith.metaDescription: The verse arrives at three in the morning and does not comfort. Under the racing heart is a worse fear: that the anxiety itself is the sin.

qa.question: Is My Anxiety a Spiritual Failure?
qa.answer: The verse arrives at three in the morning and does not come as comfort. Underneath the racing heart is a second fear, quieter and worse: that the anxiety itself is the verdict on your faith. It is not. Let me tell you why.

are-miracles-believable.metaDescription: It took me a long time to notice that my proof was a definition doing all the work. I used to think I had a proof.

qa.question: Are Miracles Believable?
qa.answer: For years I carried what I took to be a proof against miracles, borrowed from a dead Scottish philosopher, and I loved the clean feeling of the case being closed. It took me a long time to notice that my proof was a definition doing all the work.

baptism-mode-and-subjects.metaDescription: Two churches on the same street baptize with the same water and cannot agree on who should stand in it, or how deep.

qa.question: Sprinkle or Immerse? Infant or Believer?
qa.answer: Two churches on the same street baptize with the same water and cannot agree on who should stand in it, or how deep. One brings a grown convert down under a river. One brings an eight-day-old baby to a font. Both say Scripture. Both are my family. I will not settle it for you.

can-you-be-good-without-god.metaDescription: You can be good without God. I was, for years, and so are people you love.

qa.question: Can You Be Good Without God?
qa.answer: You can be good without God. I was, for years, and so are people you love. The question that kept its grip on me was quieter: what makes cruelty actually wrong, and not just a thing I happen to hate.

can-you-lose-your-salvation.metaDescription: The question does not usually arrive in a classroom. The church has answered it two ways for centuries. I am not going to close it for you.

qa.question: Can You Lose Your Salvation?
qa.answer: The question does not usually arrive in a classroom. It arrives at three in the morning, when a Christian who has failed badly lies in the dark and wonders if the door is still open. The church has answered it two ways for centuries. I am not going to close it for you. I am going to tell you the truth about both.

cessationism-or-continuation.metaDescription: I have stood in a hospital room with my hand on a dying man and waited to see if the machines would change. They did not.

qa.question: Do the Gifts Still Happen?
qa.answer: I have stood in a hospital room with my hand on a dying man and waited to see if the machines would change. They did not. I came to faith out of atheism, so the question of whether God still acts is not a doctrine I inherited. It is the seam where my old life and my new one still rub.

christian-sexual-ethic.metaDescription: A gay teenager sat in my church for three years and never told me, because he had learned exactly what we would do with it.

qa.question: Is the Historic Christian View of Sex Homophobic?
qa.answer: A gay teenager sat in my church for three years and never told me, because he had learned exactly what we would do with it. Before I say one word about the texts, I have to say that. The church earned his silence, and it is the first thing that has to be true on the page.

christianity-and-islam.metaDescription: People say the two faiths are basically the same, or that they share nothing at all. Both are ways of not having the conversation.

christians-and-abortion.metaDescription: The argument is loud because it is easy. I have been both kinds of certain. Neither one was looking at the room.

qa.question: What Should Christians Think About Abortion?
qa.answer: The argument is loud because it is easy. Two slogans, thrown past each other, by people who have already decided the other side is either a killer or a bully. I have been both kinds of certain. Neither one was looking at the room.

did-god-command-genocide.metaDescription: For years this was my strongest reason to reject the Bible, and I still think the person who reads these pages and recoils is reading them correctly.

qa.question: Did God Command Genocide?
qa.answer: For years this was my strongest reason to reject the Bible, and I still think the person who reads these pages and recoils is reading them correctly. So I will not hand you a comfort I could not accept myself.

did-the-resurrection-happen.metaDescription: Everything in Christianity hangs on one event that either happened or did not. The historical case for the resurrection, made the way a skeptic deserves.

qa.question: Did the Resurrection Actually Happen?
qa.answer: Everything in Christianity hangs on one event that either happened or didn't. Here is the historical case for the resurrection, handled the way a skeptic deserves, without the shortcuts, without the pressure, with the strongest version of the doubt left standing.

divorce-and-remarriage.metaDescription: Biblical grounds for divorce and remarriage: Moses, Jesus, and Paul read in context, four Christian views, and why no view requires staying in danger.

qa.question: What Does the Bible Say About Divorce and Remarriage?
qa.answer: Asked whether a man could divorce his wife for any cause, Jesus tightened the law of Moses and named an exception in the same breath. Read in context, the texts are harder than the culture wants and more merciful than the church has often been.

does-god-actually-exist.metaDescription: A pastor who spent years as an atheist on why he stopped: not because someone won an argument, but because his own view could not pay its bills.

qa.question: Does God Actually Exist?
qa.answer: I did not stop being an atheist because someone won an argument. I stopped because the account I was defending kept sending me a bill it could not pay.

end-of-life-and-bioethics.metaDescription: The question does not arrive in an ethics seminar. It arrives in a room with a bed in it, and a doctor with kind eyes asking what you want to do.

qa.question: Should We Keep People Alive at Any Cost?
qa.answer: The question does not arrive in an ethics seminar. It arrives in a room with a bed in it, and a doctor with kind eyes asking what you want to do. I am not going to hand you a slogan on the way in. Both sides of that door are lying to you about how hard this is.

faith-and-gender-identity.metaDescription: Before it is a debate, it is a person. The church has owed both of them something for a long time, and mostly sent an argument instead.

qa.question: What Does the Church Owe Transgender People?
qa.answer: Before it is a debate, it is a person. A teenager who cannot stand to be in the body they woke up in, and a mother in the parking lot who does not know how to keep her child alive and keep her faith at the same time. The church has owed both of them something for a long time, and mostly sent an argument instead.

faith-and-science.metaDescription: Everyone knows faith and science are at war. Here is where the conflict actually came from, and where it doesn't exist.

qa.question: Do You Have to Choose Between Faith and Science?
qa.answer: Everyone knows faith and science are at war. The trouble is that the war is largely a story invented in the nineteenth century, and the man who led the human genome project is a believer. Here is where the conflict actually came from, and where it doesn't exist.

how-to-read-genesis-one.metaDescription: The wall was never the resurrection first. It was the rocks. I rejected Christianity at the creation and never got far enough to reach the cross.

qa.question: How Should a Christian Read Genesis 1?
qa.answer: The wall was never the resurrection first. It was the rocks. I rejected Christianity at the creation and never got far enough to reach the cross. What I took for a locked door was a room with several chairs in it.

if-god-is-good-why-suffering.metaDescription: The strongest argument against God is not made by philosophers. It is made by a suffering child, and Dostoevsky put it better than any atheist since.

qa.question: If God Is Good, Why Is There So Much Suffering?
qa.answer: The strongest argument against God is not made by philosophers. It is made by a suffering child, and Dostoevsky put it better than any atheist since. Here is the problem of evil taken at full strength, no glib answers, no comfort that isn't earned.

is-faith-irrational.metaDescription: I spent years certain that faith was the enemy of reason and that I had chosen reason.

qa.question: Is Believing Anything on Faith Irrational?
qa.answer: I spent years certain that faith was the enemy of reason and that I had chosen reason. Then I noticed how much of my own position I was holding on trust, and had never once thought to check.

is-faith-just-wishful-thinking.metaDescription: For years I was certain that faith was a comfort weak people reached for because they could not bear the cold.

qa.question: Is Faith Just Wishful Thinking?
qa.answer: For years I was certain that faith was a comfort weak people reached for because they could not bear the cold. I still think that is sometimes exactly what it is. Then I noticed the wish I had never once examined: my own.

is-hell-eternal.metaDescription: It is not whether there is a hell that keeps people awake. It is whether it stops.

qa.question: Is Hell Forever, or Does It End?
qa.answer: It is not whether there is a hell that keeps people awake. It is whether it stops. There is a difference, and every grieving heart knows it, between a God who lets a soul finally cease and a God who keeps it alive forever so it can go on burning.

is-jesus-really-the-only-way.metaDescription: A former atheist on the claim he once found obscene: that Jesus is the only way. The objection at full strength, and the one question it cannot survive.

qa.question: Is Jesus Really the Only Way?
qa.answer: For most of my life I was an atheist, and of all the things the church claimed, that Jesus is the only way struck me as not merely improbable but obscene. Then I noticed the one question the parable of the blind men and the elephant cannot survive being asked.

just-war-and-pacifism.metaDescription: Two Christians read the same Sermon on the Mount. One picks up a rifle to stop a slaughter. One lays the rifle down and lets them kill him first.

meaning-without-god.metaDescription: The atheist is not the miserable nihilist the church invented to feel better. He builds real, loving, meaningful lives.

qa.question: Can a Life Mean Anything Without God?
qa.answer: The atheist is not the miserable nihilist the church invented to feel better. He builds real, loving, meaningful lives. The question is not whether he can make meaning. It is whether meaning you make can hold you when you stop believing in it.

natural-evil-and-animal-suffering.metaDescription: Free will explains the evil we do to each other. This is the objection I have never fully answered, and I will not pretend here that I finally have.

near-death-experiences.metaDescription: The tunnel, the light, the voice saying it is not yet time. As a materialist I mocked these accounts.

qa.question: Does the Evidence for Near-Death Experiences Prove Anything?

the-rise-of-the-nones.metaDescription: They are the fastest-growing 'religious' group in America, and most of them are not atheists.

exvangelical-when-leaving-isnt-losing-fa.metaDescription: A growing movement of former evangelicals is redefining what it means to leave a tradition without leaving the faith that tradition claimed to own.

purity-culture-and-its-wreckage.metaDescription: A generation was taught that their sexual worth was a commodity to be preserved.

prosperity-gospel-is-not-the-gospel.metaDescription: The inquiry produced no legislation. By any serious theological standard it is also a heresy.

when-politics-replaced-theology.metaDescription: The story of how American evangelicalism traded its prophetic voice for political power is not the story most evangelicals have been told.

religious-trauma-is-real.metaDescription: For millions of people, the most damaging experiences of their lives happened in the name of God.

spiritual-abuse-how-good-theology-gets-w.metaDescription: Spiritual abuse does not require bad theology. The church's vulnerability to this dynamic is a structural problem, not merely a personnel one.

why-young-adults-arent-coming-back.metaDescription: The church has spent two decades trying to make itself more appealing to young adults.

is-god-real.metaDescription: The question of God's existence deserves more than slogans from either side.

why-does-god-allow-suffering.metaDescription: The problem of suffering is not an intellectual puzzle to be solved. The question arrives not in a seminar room but in a hospital corridor.

qa.question: Why Does God Allow Suffering?
qa.answer: The problem of suffering is not an intellectual puzzle to be solved. It is a wound that demands not explanation but presence, and the Christian answer begins at the cross, where God enters the wound.

can-you-trust-the-bible.metaDescription: The Bible is not what most people think it is, on either side of the argument. It is stranger, more honest, and tougher than the stories told about it.

qa.question: Can You Trust the Bible?
qa.answer: The Bible is not what most people think it is, defenders and critics alike. It is stranger, more varied, more honest, and more resilient than either the fundamentalist or the skeptic imagines.

what-christians-believe-about-hell.metaDescription: The Christian tradition has never spoken with one voice about hell. So this is not an argument for a single position.

science-and-faith-are-not-at-war.metaDescription: The story is so deeply set in Western culture that it feels like a fact: science and religion have always been at war, and science has been winning.

evolution-and-genesis.metaDescription: The debate over evolution and Genesis has generated more heat than light for over a century.

the-historical-jesus.metaDescription: The quest for the historical Jesus has occupied scholars for over two centuries.

do-miracles-still-happen.metaDescription: The question of miracles is not whether they violate natural law. I hold both, and this essay is written from between them.

qa.question: Miracles: Do They Still Happen?
qa.answer: The question of miracles is not whether they violate natural law. It is whether the universe is the kind of place where the unexpected can break through, and whether we are the kind of people willing to notice.

why-christianity.metaDescription: The question is not whether Christianity is the only religion with truth in it.

qa.question: Why Christianity and Not Something Else?
qa.answer: The question is not whether Christianity is the only religion with truth in it. The question is whether it makes claims that are unique, claims that matter, and claims that can bear the weight of a life.

the-problem-with-certainty.metaDescription: The demand for certainty is not a sign of strong faith. We have made certainty the measure of faith, and it is destroying us.

how-to-talk-about-faith.metaDescription: Most Christians have been trained to share their faith in ways that guarantee nobody wants to hear it. The problem is not the gospel.

raising-kids-post-christian.metaDescription: Your children will not inherit your faith by osmosis. There is a moment every Christian parent dreads, though few admit it out loud.

faith-at-work.metaDescription: The office is not a mission field. The average American spends about 90,000 hours at work over a lifetime.

interfaith-marriage.metaDescription: What the Bible says to a Christian thinking of marrying an unbeliever, and to one already married: 2 Corinthians 6, 1 Corinthians 7 and 1 Peter 3.

digital-discipleship.metaDescription: The algorithm is not neutral. It is forming you into a particular kind of person, distracted, reactive, shallow, and perpetually outraged.

finding-a-good-church.metaDescription: The search for a good church is not about finding perfection. The person who has been hurt by a church occupies a uniquely painful position.

family-and-faith-transitions.metaDescription: Faith transitions do not happen in isolation. They happen in families. And the family that cannot hold theological difference cannot hold each other.

christianity-after-christendom.metaDescription: The era when Christianity was the cultural default is over. What comes next may be harder, smaller, and more costly.

the-spirituality-of-doubt.metaDescription: Doubt is not the opposite of faith. It is faith doing its hardest work. And the Christian tradition has always known this, even when the church forgot.

reconstructing-faith.metaDescription: Deconstruction is not the destination. It is the demolition phase of a renovation.

sexual-abuse-crisis-in-the-church.metaDescription: The abuse crisis is not a Catholic problem or a Protestant problem. It is a power problem.

why-the-church-lost-the-culture-war.metaDescription: The church spent forty years trying to win a culture war it was never meant to fight. The cost was not just political defeat.

white-evangelicalism-and-race.metaDescription: The American church did not merely tolerate slavery. It theologized it.

megachurch-model.metaDescription: The megachurch movement reached millions and revealed something important about American Christianity's hunger for accessibility.

church-and-mental-health.metaDescription: The church that tells a depressed person to pray harder is not offering spiritual counsel. It is practicing spiritual malpractice.

toxic-masculinity-in-the-pulpit.metaDescription: The church that confuses aggression with authority and domination with leadership has not recovered biblical manhood.

colonialism-and-missions.metaDescription: The cross arrived in the colonies alongside the sword. That refusal is itself a theological failure.

what-christians-can-learn-from-judaism.metaDescription: Christianity emerged from Judaism and then spent two millennia pretending it had outgrown its parent.

what-christians-can-learn-from-islam.metaDescription: Islam is the faith Christians know least and fear most. That fear has produced ignorance, and that ignorance has impoverished both traditions.

what-christians-can-learn-from-buddhism.metaDescription: The contemplative traditions of Christianity and Buddhism have been carrying on a quiet conversation for centuries.

what-christians-can-learn-from-indigenou.metaDescription: The church that destroyed indigenous traditions in the name of Christ had much to learn from the very people it sought to convert.

the-christian-mystics.metaDescription: The Christian mystical tradition is not an esoteric footnote to the faith.
